messages.subject: Re: Transition guide from 0.8.9 to 0.9.0
parts:
Hi Dennis,

Awesome job, thanks!
Looking at the code I have a couple of suggestions:

- use the jpeg package to read Hadley's picture. It's probably easier
to install than ReadImages (no system dependency).
http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/jpeg/index.html
The function is called readJPG()

- the R script file looks like it was manually put together. I think
you have two options that might be useful (especially for updates):
tangle from the knitr document (use purl('guide.Rnw') instead of
knit('guide.Rnw')), or use the externalization of code chunks
(http://yihui.name/knitr/demo/externalization/) where you put
references ##@knitr chunk1 in an external R file, and call them by
name <<chunk1>>@ in the .Rnw document.

- use an incremental, unique indicator for each new plot, e.g. p1, p2,
p3, p4, ... (at least for the major specimen) so that we can refer to
a specific plot in the absence of figure captions in the document.

- the R logo is stretched; perhaps it's a good place to use
annotation_custom(rasterGrob(Rlogo), xmin= 8, xmax = 10, ymin = 2,
ymax = 3) instead, which will preserve the aspect ratio (unless you
specify both width and height in rasterGrob()).

- I can imagine that some people (I did) might try to copy and paste
code from the pdf document. This will often fail to run because of the
fancy quotes. I'm not sure how best to fix this (short of using
XeTeX), perhaps options(useFancyQuotes = FALSE) would help, or
http://stackoverflow.com/a/1663936/471093 if it's a problem on the
LaTeX side.

All the best,

b.


On 14 February 2012 11:54, Dennis Murphy <djm...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Greetings:
>
> As many of you know, there is a new version of ggplot2 that has been
> threatening to come out for the past few months. The anticipated
> release date is March 1 if everything goes well with CRAN. Over the
> past few weeks, I've been putting together a document, overseen by
> development group members, that I hope will ease the transition from
> ggplot2-0.8.9 to ggplot2-0.9.0. It covers the following topics:
>    * basic changes in the package
>    * new geoms
>    * the new guides functionality that will give users more control
> over the appearance of legend guides
>    * a couple of new features in facet_grid()
>    * examples using the new annotation functions
>    * some coverage of the recent scales package and how it can be
> used with ggplot2
>    * lots of examples and pretty pictures :)
>
> The document is attached to this mail, but discussions are ongoing as
> to where it will have a more permanent home. I will let you know when
> the location is determined, so that future updates can be cited rather
> than attached as mail entries.
>
> To run the code in this document, you'll need the development versions
> of ggplot2 and scales. You will also need to have the following
> packages installed from CRAN: plyr, reshape2, rgdal, maps, maptools,
> rgeos, MASS, gridExtra and ReadImages. If you're not already using the
> development version ggplot2-0.9.0 and you want to try out the code in
> the document (also attached), here's how to get it:
>
> (1) Install the devtools package from CRAN.
> (2) [Optional...I think] Install Rtools from CRAN, in the same place
> you grab the distribution binaries for your platform. (See the rtools
> subdirectory.) Since neither ggplot2 nor scales uses any external C or
> C++ code, this step may not be necessary.
> (3) In a fresh R session:
>
> library('devtools')
> dev_mode()     # should reply dev_mode: ON - if not, do it again.
> ## only works if dev_mode is ON:
>
> install_github("ggplot2")
> install_github("scales")
>
> # If both packages install without errors, then
> library('ggplot2')    # note that plyr, reshape, etc. are NOT loaded!
> library('scales')
>
> ...and start copying and pasting the code from the attached R file
> into the session to replicate the plots. (Don't forget to load the
> required packages first - they are not loaded inside the script.) If
> the installation goes ka-bong, then try installing Rtools and repeat
> step 3 above. On Windows, it's probably safer if you start the R
> session by running it as Administrator.
>
> The document was typeset using the recently released knitr package by
> Yihui Xie. If you like the way it looks, visit the package website at
> yihui.name/knitr. I highly recommend it. (And thanks to Josh Wiley for
> turning me onto it in December.)
>
> Feedback and suggestions welcomed; if questions or problems arise,
> don't be shy about asking. The objective is to have a working document
> ready to go a few days before the release date.
>
> I hope you find this guide useful as you move from ggplot2-0.8.9 to 0.9.0.
>
> On behalf of the ggplot2 developers,
> Dennis
>

what already works and would take more time than it's worth for this
project.

Actually, the logo looked like that in the original full sized plot :)
I need to adjust ymax a bit to align it properly. I'll play with
rasterGrob(), too; does that require grid?

>

> LaTeX side.

I thought I got rid of those by replacing them with double quotes, but
that was before the annotation section was added. Force of
habit...sigh. I'll go over those again.

Best regards,
Dennis

>

>
> b.

In knitr you can specify which lines you'd like to have echoed, e.g
echo=-4 will not show the 4th line in the output document. This way
you can hide some portions of the code chunk and still show others.
